 By Tom Kao November 4, 2026 Already hooked on Disney+'s "The Remarried Empress" and counting down the days until the next episodes? If you're looking for something to watch in the meantime, why not revisit some of Lee Jong-suk's most memorable K-dramas? From playing a wealthy webtoon character in "W" to a lawyer caught up in a dangerous conspiracy in "Big Mouth," the actor has taken on quite a variety of roles over the years. Whether you're in the mood for a heartwarming romance, a fantasy adventure or a gripping thriller, here are eight Lee Jong-suk K-dramas worth adding to your watchlist 
 W: Two Worlds Apart (2016)
 What happens when a fictional character discovers he's living inside a webtoon? In W: Two Worlds Apart , Lee Jong-suk plays Kang Chul, a wealthy businessman and former Olympic shooting champion whose life takes an unexpected turn when Oh Yeon-joo (Han Hyo-joo), a surgeon from the real world, mysteriously enters his universe. After saving him from a near-fatal attack, Yeon-joo finds herself repeatedly pulled into the webtoon created by her missing father. As romance blossoms between them, the line between fiction and reality begins to blur, bringing unexpected dangers to both worlds.
 While You Were Sleeping (2017)
 Imagine being able to see the future in your dreams, only to realise that some of your worst nightmares might come true. While You Were Sleeping follows Nam Hong-joo (Bae Suzy), a young woman who dreams of tragic events before they happen but struggles to prevent them. Things begin to change when her new neighbour, rookie prosecutor Jung Jae-chan (Lee Jong-suk), has a dream that helps him save her life. Together with police officer Han Woo-tak (Jung Hae-in), who develops the same ability, they team up to prevent tragedies and uncover dangerous secrets.
 Pinocchio (2014)
 One of Lee Jong-suk's breakthrough dramas, Pinocchio follows Choi Dal-po, originally named Ki Ha-myeong, whose family was torn apart by misleading news reports following a tragic fire. After growing up under a new identity, he decides to become a reporter to uncover the truth behind his family's downfall. Along the way, he develops feelings for fellow aspiring journalist Choi In-ha (Park Shin-hye), who has an unusual condition that causes her to hiccup whenever she lies. There's just one complication: her mother is the reporter responsible for ruining his family, putting their budding romance to the test.

 Big Mouth (2022)
 Taking a darker turn from his usual romantic roles, Lee Jong-suk plays Park Chang-ho, an unsuccessful lawyer with a dismal 10% win rate in Big Mouth . After taking on a high-profile murder case, he is framed as the notorious criminal mastermind Big Mouse and thrown into a dangerous prison. To stay alive, Chang-ho begins pretending to be the very criminal he's accused of being, gradually gaining influence among the inmates. Meanwhile, his wife, Go Mi-ho (Im Yoon-ah), investigates the conspiracy outside, determined to clear his name and expose the powerful figures pulling the strings.
 Romance Is a Bonus Book (2019)
 For something a little more lighthearted, Romance Is a Bonus Book follows Cha Eun-ho (Lee Jong-suk), a successful writer and the youngest editor-in-chief at a publishing company. His longtime friend Kang Dan-yi (Lee Na-young), a divorced single mother struggling to restart her career, secretly works as his housekeeper while hiding her financial troubles. After landing a job at his company by concealing her previous experience, Dan-yi slowly gets back on her feet. Meanwhile, Eun-ho's long-hidden feelings for her begin to surface, turning their longtime friendship into a sweet, slow-burning romance.
 I Hear Your Voice (2013)
 Another of Lee Jong-suk's early hits, I Hear Your Voice follows Park Soo-ha, a high school student who gains the ability to read minds after witnessing his father's murder. Ten years later, he reunites with Jang Hye-sung (Lee Bo-young), a cynical public defender whose childhood testimony helped convict the killer. Determined to protect her, Soo-ha uses his unusual ability to help her solve legal cases, with their relationship gradually developing into something more. However, when the murderer is released from prison and returns for revenge, the two find themselves in serious danger.
 Doctor Stranger (2014)
 In Doctor Stranger , Lee Jong-suk plays Park Hoon, a brilliant surgeon who was taken to North Korea as a child alongside his father and trained to become a doctor. After escaping to South Korea, he begins working at a prestigious hospital while desperately searching for his lost love, Song Jae-hee (Jin Se-yeon), who was separated from him during their escape. Things take a mysterious turn when he encounters a doctor who looks exactly like her but claims not to recognise him, drawing him into fierce medical rivalries and dangerous political conspiracies.
 Law and the City (2025)
 One of Lee Jong-suk's more recent dramas, Law and the City follows five associate lawyers navigating their careers and personal lives in Seoul's busy Seocho legal district. Lee plays Ahn Ju-hyeong, a highly capable but somewhat cynical lawyer who has spent nine years at the same firm. His predictable routine takes an unexpected turn when he reunites with Kang Hui-ji (Mun Ka-young), a passionate junior lawyer with whom he shared a brief romance in Hong Kong ten years earlier. As old feelings resurface, the two navigate demanding cases, workplace friendships and their different approaches to justice.
